title: Interlocks
summary: Prevent combinations that damage equipment: a pump must not run dry, a valve and a pump must not fight each other.

sections.heading: Protecting the process
sections.body: An **interlock** blocks or stops equipment when a condition makes operation unsafe for the equipment or the product. A **permissive** must be TRUE to start; a **trip** stops running equipment.

sections.heading: Interlocks around a pump
sections.body: The drain pump needs liquid in the tank.
sections.diagram:
DrainRequest ---+
                  AND --> DrainPump
  NOT LevelLow ---+
  (pump runs only when the tank is above the low switch)

sections.heading: Pump with dry-run protection
sections.body: LevelLow is TRUE while the tank is below the low switch.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Adding the interlock to only one of several places that start the pump. Calculate a single permit and use it everywhere.

question.question: 'The pump must not start below the low level and must stop when the level drops below it.' What is LevelLow?
options: Both a permissive and a trip
question.explanation: It blocks the start and stops a running pump.

sections.heading: Practice: batch sequence
sections.body: The fill-and-drain sequence must never run the pump dry and never run valve and pump together.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
Interlocks protect equipment; calculate them once and AND them into every run condition. People are protected by separate safety systems.

**Troubleshooting note:** A device that refuses to start without an alarm is often blocked by an interlock; check every condition in its permit.
